subject: Problem in reading files stored in HDFS

messages.author: da2ca011efc9d511
messages.subject: Problem in reading files stored in HDFS
parts:
Hi,

I am confused about accessing files stored in HDFS (uploaded by some other program e.g. Hadoop command line utility) from R using rmr packages.
I am trying to explain with an example.
Say I have two csv files (For simplicity I have taken csv files more complex for binary files)
One is a.csv and other is b.csv
Initially both are residing in local filesystem.
I'll upload these files in HDFS one through R and one through command line.
Once those are stored in HDFS I would like to read the content of the files from R.
Here goes the first case.

===========================================
to.dfs("a.csv", output="/user/hduser/a.csv")
read.csv(values(from.dfs("/user/hduser/a.csv"))[1][[1]]) # reads the csv file correctly
===========================================

Now let me upload the b.csv from command line.

===========================================
$ /usr/local/hadoop/bin/hadoop dfs -copyFromLocal b.csv /user/hduser/b.csv
===========================================

Now if I try to read the file from R like

===========================================
read.csv(values(from.dfs("/user/hduser/b.csv"))[1][[1]]) # failed to read the file
===========================================

It fails to read the files.
Rather it reads the several key, value pairs (Keys I can not correlate, It is an non-sequential increasing series and Values are lines of the CSV file.
Note: For binary files it seems a chunk of the file is returned for each key

I understand that the way R puts the file in HDFS and the command line does are different and hence the issue.
But there must be an mechanism from R to read the files stored in HDFS by non-R programs (Like command line).

I tried to use hdfs://master_node_ip_address:50075/user/hduser/b.csv but it fails.

In Java you can do like this Path pt=new Path("hdfs://ip_address:port/user/hduser/b.csv")
I am not a Java expert but this probably works (I googled and found such things).

Now I clearly understands the in Java there are surely libraries which know how to interpret hdfs://path_to_files.

In R how to do it?

Now why do I need this. Say these filenames are stored in HBase and I want to read each file within Mapreduce program.

Please do advise and feel free to get back to me in case of any question.

Thanks and regards,
Souvik.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#227] Problem in reading files stored in HDFS
parts:
help(from.dfs) and 5 minutes of intense, focused reading will give you more value that any of your experiments. I hope other users are not confused by reading your code -- I was. Check out rhdfs if you want some of the hadoop dfs functionality from R. In particular rmr adopts a two layer memory model, and none of the existing backends can access both the local file system and hdfs.


Antonio

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#232] Problem in reading files stored in HDFS
parts: But what if I need to call a function within map function which takes the filename and the file is in HDFS.

The input has to be provided as input argument  to the mapreduce function, not performed from within the map function. That may be legal code but performance-wise is not going to get you anywhere. No IO in the map function unless you really know what you are doing.

Antonio
